10th July, 1941.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMANDER）

American Consulate-General,
131, Kiangse Road,
Shanghai

Sirs:

For your information, two incidents of potential Japanese
interference with our communications system have arisen within the
course of the past week.

Our chief watchman this morning reported that four Japanese subjects
dressed in civilian clothes and driving an automobile carrying the
license No.3321, visited our transmitting station, situated at
No.1325-A Gordon Road, next door to the Pootoo Road Police Station,
at 9.30 o'clock last night. These men remained in the vicinity
for approximately 15 minutes, according to our watchman's report,
and although they made no effort to enter the compound, they
subjected the station and the transmitting antennae to a thorough
scrutiny.

Less than a week ago three Japanese civilians arrived in the same
automobile, or at any rate an automobile bearing the same license
plates, and likewise surveyed the building from several angles for
15 or 20 minutes before driving away.

As you know, No.1325-A Gordon Road is within the jurisdiction of
the Municipal Settlement, and also is within the American Defense
Sector.

Several minor incidents of this nature have occurred in the past,
and we wish to keep you informed in the event of any further
occurrences.

先生们：

供贵方知悉，在过去一周内，发生了两起日本人可能干扰我方通信系统的事件。

我方首席看守今晨报告称，昨晚9时30分，四名身着便服、驾驶牌照号为3321汽车的日本籍人士，造访了位于戈登路1325-A号（普陀路巡捕房隔壁）的我方发射站。据我方看守报告，这些人在附近逗留了约15分钟，虽然他们并未试图进入院内，但对发射站及发射天线进行了仔细 scrutinizing（审视/检查）。

不到一周前，三名日本平民乘坐同一辆汽车，或至少是悬挂相同牌照的汽车抵达，同样从多个角度对该建筑观察了15至20分钟后驾车离去。

如贵方所知，戈登路1325-A号位于公共租界管辖范围内，同时也处于美方防区之内。

过去曾发生过数起此类轻微事件，若再发生类似情况，我方希望能随时向贵方通报。

21st April, 1941.

American Consulate-General,
Kiangse Road,
Shanghai.

Sirs:

Several months ago we received notice from the landlord of our
Transmitting Station at House No.23, Lane 455 Bubbling Well Road that
our lease (expiring on March 1st) would not be renewed.

As we were not able to rent a suitable house for our transmitters, we
were forced to lease a piece of land and construct a building thereon.
This building, located at No.1325A Gordon Road, next door to the
Pootoo Road Police Station, should be finished by the end of this month
when we expect to move all our transmitting equipment from our present
location.

In order to keep the record clear, I am reporting herein an incident of
potential Japanese interference. As you know, I have reported
several minor incidents in the past.

Despite the fact that No.1325A Gordon Road is in the Municipal Settle-
ment, within the American Defense Sector, yesterday, April 20th, two
Japanese dressed in civilian clothes tried to enter the yard where the
workmen were erecting our building and, upon being denied admittance,
they walked across the street and took several pictures of the work in
progress. As they spoke only Japanese, the workmen were not able to
understand what they had to say.

I will keep you informed as to any further occurance of this nature. I
will advise you when we definitely move into our new location.

（印：... SPECIAL SHANGHAI ... 21 APR 1941）

Respectfully,

A.R. LUSEY

数月前，我们收到位于静安寺路455弄23号的我方发射站房东的通知，称我们的租约（于3月1日到期）将不再续租。

由于我们无法为发射机租到合适的房屋，被迫租赁了一块土地并在其上建造房屋。该建筑位于戈登路1325A号，紧邻普陀路巡捕房，预计将于本月底完工，届时我们将把所有发射设备从现址搬迁至此。

为了保持记录清晰，我在此报告一起日本人可能进行干扰的事件。如贵方所知，我过去曾报告过几起轻微事件。

尽管戈登路1325A号位于公共租界内的美方防区，但在昨天，即4月20日，两名身着便服的日本人试图进入工人们正在 erecting（搭建）我方建筑的院子，在被拒绝入内后，他们走到马路对面，对施工情况进行了拍照。由于他们只讲日语，工人们无法理解他们所说的话。

如有进一步此类事件发生，我将随时向贵方通报。待我们确切搬入新址时，我将通知贵方。

Subject Joseph Kruta (German) - proposal to install radio transmitter at
Room 6, The Towers Boarding House, 1182 Avenue Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

Information has been received from D.S.I. Hillhouse
(Louza) who resides in the Towers Boarding House, 1182
Avenue Road, to the effect that the occupant of Room 6
of the aforesaid boarding house, a German, Joseph KRUTA,
had, on 11.6.40, approached the Manageress of the
boarding house, Mrs. Lupton (British) with a request
for permission to install a radio transmitter on the
verandah of Room 6. Mrs. Lupton replied that she
would require time to consider the matter and on the
night of 12.6.40, informed Kruta that permission could
not be granted. Kruta then endeavoured to explain to
Mrs. Lupton that she had misunderstood him, that he had
never mentioned "radio transmitter" but merely desired
to erect an ordinary antenna for a receiving set.

Enquiries by the Special Branch reveal that Joseph
KRUTA is employed by Siemssen & Co. and that he arrived
in Shanghai on 28.4.40 from South China. He is listed
in the German Hong List as Joseph Kaufmann Kruta,
Siemssen & Co., 75 Shameen, B.C., P.O. Box 57, Canton
(15 Tah Do Lo, Tel. 70147).

Another German, the occupant of Room 5 of the Towers
and a daily visitor in Kruta's room is one Erik Ammann,
described as a merchant, who came to the Towers on
23.4.40. This person was formerly employed by The
K.D. Petroleum Co. of China, French Bank Building, P.O.
Box 870, Hongkong. He is known to spend most of his time
in the Cafe Federal.

D.C.(Special Br.)

由警探长洛根 (D.S.I. Logan) 制作并转呈

收到居住在爱文义路1182号塔楼公寓的警探长希尔豪斯 (D.S.I. Hillhouse)（Louza）的情报，称上述公寓6号房间的住客、德国人约瑟夫·克鲁塔 (Joseph KRUTA) 于1940年6月11日向公寓女经理、英国人拉普顿夫人 (Mrs. Lupton) 提出请求，希望在6号房间的阳台上安装一台无线电发射机。拉普顿夫人回答说她需要时间考虑此事，并于1940年6月12日晚告知克鲁塔，不予批准。克鲁塔随后试图向拉普顿夫人解释说她误会了他，他从未提及“无线电发射机”，而只是想为接收机架设一根普通天线。

经特务科调查，约瑟夫·克鲁塔受雇于西门子洋行 (Siemssen & Co.)，他于1940年4月28日从华南抵达上海。他在德国鸿名册 (German Hong List) 中登记为约瑟夫·考夫曼·克鲁塔 (Joseph Kaufmann Kruta)，西门子洋行，广州沙面75号，邮政信箱57号（大道路15号，电话70147）。

另一名德国人，塔楼公寓5号房间的住客，且是克鲁塔房间的日常访客，名为埃里克·阿曼 (Erik Ammann)，职业描述为商人，于1940年4月23日来到塔楼公寓。此人此前受雇于中国煤油公司 (The K.D. Petroleum Co. of China)，地址为香港法国银行大楼，邮政信箱870号。据悉他大部分时间都在联邦咖啡馆 (Cafe Federal) 度过。

CHINA DAILY NEWS

MAY 21 1940

International Radio
Warfare in Shanghai
“Black Chambers” to
Steal Secret Messages

Shanghai’s telegraph and radio offices have worked overtime recently to handle the rush of messages to and from Europe and America which have resulted from the European war, the “Tairiku Shimpo” reported yesterday.

At the Shanghai International Radio office the number of messages between this city and Rome and Berlin, only two points in Europe with which service is maintained, has increased by 600 per cent. in the last few weeks, the paper said. The daily average of messages sent to Rome is now about 40 while 30 go to Berlin.

The Great Northern Telegraph Co., the Eastern Extension Telegraph Co. and the Commercial Pacific Cable Co. are also reported to be busy.

Over 230 messages between here and American cities are handled by the R.C.A. Communications Co. and the Mackay Radio and Telegraph Co., the paper reported, of which almost two thirds are outgoing cables.

The “Tairiku” observed that lack of official control over radio communication in Shanghai has given rise to international radio warfare here as diplomatic and military authorities of foreign nations operate their own radio services.

An official of the Shanghai International Radio office told a reporter from the paper that important diplomatic messages seldom pass through the ordinary commercial channels.

He added that authorities of various nations have established “Black chambers” here “to steal the secret messages,” the paper said.

《字林西报》

1940年5月21日

国际无线电
在上海的战争
“黑室”窃取
秘密电文

据《大陆新报》昨日报道，由于欧洲战争导致往来欧美之间的电报激增，上海的电信和无线电办事处最近一直在加班处理这些业务。

该报称，在上海国际无线电公司，本市与罗马和柏林之间（这是欧洲仅存的两个保持服务的地点）的电报数量在过去几周内增加了600%。目前每天发往罗马的电报平均约为40份，发往柏林的为30份。

据报道，大北电报公司、大东电报公司和太平洋商业电缆公司也业务繁忙。

该报报道， RCA 通信公司和麦凯无线电电报公司处理了此处与美国城市之间的230多份电报，其中近三分之二为去程电报。

《大陆新报》指出，由于上海缺乏对无线电通信的官方管制，各国外交和军事当局自行运营无线电服务，导致此地出现了国际无线电战。

上海国际无线电公司的一名官员告诉该报记者，重要的外交电文很少通过普通的商业渠道传递。

该报称，他补充说，各国当局已在此设立“黑室”以“窃取秘密电文”。

（批注：51 / fu 5月21日）
（批注：归档 / 80½）

Suspicious behaviour of one Japanese and two Chinese
outside Bentleys Ltd., Press Wireless and Globe Wireless
Radio Stations on May 13, 1940.

At 10.45 a.m. May 13, 1940, Mr. Marco,
Manager of Bentleys Ltd., 18 The Bund, telephoned to
D.S.I. Logan and reported that one Japanese in company
with two Chinese, one of whom was identified as the
chief radio man of the Wang Ching Wei clique in
Shanghai, were seen about 10 a.m. May 13, 1940 acting
in a suspicious manner outside the following radio

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached communication
containing a report to the effect that a certain Chinese,
YANG TEH CHAO, has established a secret Wireless Trans-
mitting Station at No.73 Hwa Kee Avenue, Bubbling Well
Road, with a view to supporting the activities of the
Wang Ching Wei Regime; discreet enquiries made have
failed to confirm this information.

Investigations show that one Sz Yi Ni is the
owner of a boarding house at House 73. Hwa Kee Avenue,
which consists of 13 rooms, all sub-let to different
individuals. None of the occupants answers to the name
of YANG TEH CHAO but there is one named YOUNG SZE CHAN
(楊世昌) alias YANG SING DZ (楊心如), who is at
present employed in the Statistical Department of the
Chinese Maritime Customs. He is a doctor by profession
who formerly practiced in Hankow, and after the fall of
Hankow proceeded to Hongkong and arrived in Shanghai in
January, 1939. Being for some reason unable to
establish a paying practice here, he entered the Customs
on April 8th, 1939. There is no information to the
effect that he is interested in any political movement.

By discreet arrangement, the various rooms in
House 73 Hwa Kee Avenue have been inspected but there is
no sign of a transmitter being installed in any part of
the building.

R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S. I.

DATED NOVEMBER 25, 1939
CONFIDENTIAL

Group of pro-WANG CHING WEI agents attempt
to sabotage Havas News Agency Radio Trans-
mitting Station at 353 Rue Cardinal Mercier.

At 8 a.m. November 25, acting on information
supplied by one YANG NING KENG ( 楊 銀 根 ), aged 23,
a native of Wusih, employed as a coolie in the Havas
News Agency Radio Transmitting Station at 353 Rue
Cardinal Mercier, a French Police patrol arrested at
the corner of Mercier-vallen the following individuals :-
(1) CHANG CHIH FAN ( 章 士 範 ), aged 29, native of
Wusih, residing at No.3 Hwa Tsun Li, Jessfield Road,
a member of the special group of the Headquarters of
the Special Service Section located at 76 Jessfield
Road - the pro-WANG CHING WEI gang.
(2) LI DAH ZI ( 李 大 全 ), aged 39, native of
Li-sui, Kiangsu, residing at 29 Chien Ka Heng,
Jessfield Road, employed in the same manner as (1).
At about 7.30 a.m. to-day, the two above
persons, profiting by the fact that the door of 353
Rue Cardinal Mercier had been left open by two smahs,
entered the premises and went into a back-room on the
back floor, where the Havas News Agency transmitting
station located.
While CHANG CHIH FAN, armed with a pistol,
held up the coolie YANG NING KENG under threats, his
accomplice upset and took out four tubes from the
transmitter and placed in the interior of the apparatus
a cigarette box containing an explosive.
These various operations having come to a
finish, the two of them left taking with them the coolie.

The first is an ex-member of the Central Tangpu

SZE TAH YU gave them instructions yesterday

At 7 p.m. yesterday, under the guidance of

上述两人在我们的指纹局中没有前科记录。

30 /11 39

Group of pro-WANG CHING WEI agents attempt
to sabotage Havas News Agency Radio Trans-
mitting Station at 353 Rue Cardinal Mercier.

At 8 a.m. November 25, acting on information
supplied by one YANG NING KENG ( 楊銀根 ), aged 23,
a native of Wusih, employed as a coolie in the Havas
News Agency Radio Transmitting Station at 353 Rue
Cardinal Mercier, a French Police patrol arrested at
the corner of Mercier-vallon the following individuals :-
(1) CHANG CHIH FAN ( 章士範 ), aged 29, native of
Wusih, residing at No.3 Hwa Tsun Li, Jessfield Road,
a member of the special group of the Headquarters of
the Special Service Section located at 76 Jessfield
Road - the pro-WANG CHING WEI gang.
(2) LI DAH ZI ( 李大全 ), aged 39, native of
Li-sui, Kiangsu, residing at 29 Chien Ka Heng,
Jessfield Road, employed in the same manner as (1).

At about 7.30 a.m. to-day, the two above
persons, profiting by the fact that the door of 353
Rue Cardinal Mercier had been left open by two amahs,
entered the premises and went into a back-room on the
back floor, where the Havas News Agency transmitting
station located.

While CHANG CHIH FAN, armed with a pistol,
held up the coolie YANG NING KENG under threats, his
accomplice upset and took out four tubes from the
transmitter and placed in the interior of the apparatus
a cigarette box containing an explosive.

These various operations having come to a
finish, the two of them left taking with them the coolie.

11月25日上午8时，根据杨银根（YANG NING KENG）提供的
情报，杨银根，23岁，无锡人，受雇于梅神父路353号哈瓦斯
通讯社无线电发射站，担任苦力，法国警察巡逻队在梅神父路
与瓦隆路（Mercier-vallon）拐角处逮捕了以下人员：-
(1) 章士範（CHANG CHIH FAN），29岁，无锡人，住极司菲尔
路华村里3号，系极司菲尔路76号特别服务处总部特别小组成员——
即亲汪精卫帮派。
(2) 李大全（LI DAH ZI），39岁，江苏溧水人，住极司菲尔路
钱家衡29号，受雇情况同(1)。

今日上午7时30分左右，上述两人利用353号梅神父路大门
被两名女佣（amahs）敞开的机会，进入该处所，并进入后楼的
一间后屋，哈瓦斯通讯社发射站即位于此处。

当章士範持手枪威胁并控制苦力杨银根时，其同伙弄倒
发射机，取出四个电子管，并在仪器内部放置了一个装有炸药的
香烟盒。

完成上述各项操作后，两人带着苦力离开。

page_data.en:
( 2 )

A little later, the latter, having succeeded in making
his escape, gave the alarm to the police officers who,
after pursuit, managed to arrest the two fugitives.

Interrogated, CHANG CHIH FAN and LI DAH ZIE,
made the following statements to us :-

The first is an ex-member of the Central Tangpu
of the Nationalist Government, and of the propaganda
section of the Kuomintang Party in Chungking.

The second is a former translator of telegrams
in the Ming Kuo Jih Pao, which has been closed since the
start of the hostilities.

Both have been present employed as probationary
members during the past two months at 76 Jessfield Road
under the orders of one SZE TAH YU ( 施大遇 ) , subor-
dinate of TING ME TSUENG ( 丁默邨 ). They state that
have no determined mission or leaning.

SZE TAH YU gave them instructions yesterday
to proceed to the Navas station and also gave them this
morning the pistol and grenade. The instigator informed
them that this station was a Nationalist Government
intelligence agency.

At 7 p.m. yesterday, under the guidance of
SZE, LI DAH ZIE went to reconnoitre the locale.

This morning they made their way to the corner
of Vallon-Mercier in a Ford Hire car driven by chauffeur
CHOW SIAO MAO ( 周小毛 ). The latter came to Central
Station and made a written statement.

The two persons in question have no previous in
our Finger Print Bureau.

The grenade which contained a powerful explosive
has been destroyed by Sergeant-Chief CHAILLOUX.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )

稍后，后者成功逃脱，并向警员报警，警员经追捕后，成功逮捕了两名逃犯。

经讯问，章士範（CHANG CHIH FAN）和李大金（LI DAH ZIE）向我们作了如下陈述：

前者系国民政府中央党部及国民党重庆宣传部的前成员。

后者系《民国日报》（Ming Kuo Jih Pao）的前电报翻译员，该报自战事爆发以来已停刊。

过去两个月，两人均在极司菲尔路76号受施大遇（SZE TAH YU）之命担任试用成员，施大遇系丁默邨（TING ME TSUENG）的下属。他们声称没有确定的任务或倾向。

施大遇昨日指示他们前往纳瓦斯电台（Navas station），并于今晨向他们提供了手枪和手榴弹。指使者告知他们，该电台是国民政府的情报机构。

昨晚7时，在施的引导下，李大金前往侦察现场。

今晨，他们乘坐由司机周小毛（CHOW SIAO MAO）驾驶的福特租赁汽车，前往麦尔西爱路与瓦隆路路口。随后，该司机前往中央捕房并提交了书面供词。

上述两人在本局指纹局均无前科记录。

装有强力炸药的手榴弹已由夏尤（CHAILLOUX）警长销毁。

5/T

事由：汪精卫集团特工企图破坏位于麦尔西爱路353号的“哈瓦斯”通讯社无线电发射台。

参考：中日敌对行动。
恐怖主义。
汪精卫集团的活动。

11月25日8时，根据一名叫杨银根（YANG NING KENG）的男子的指认，该男子23岁，无锡人，系位于麦尔西爱路353号的“哈瓦斯”通讯社无线电报发射台的苦力，法国警察巡逻队（1）在麦尔西爱路与瓦隆路路口逮捕了以下人员：
1/- 章士範（CHANG CHIH FAN），29岁，无锡人，住址为极司菲尔路华村3号，系设于极司菲尔路76号的特种工作参谋部特别科成员——该机构为亲汪精卫组织。
2/- 李大金（LI DAH ZI），39岁，江苏溧水人，住址为极司菲尔路建嘉恒29号，职务同上。

当日约7时30分，上述两人趁麦尔西爱路353号房屋前门刚被两名阿妈打开之机，潜入该住宅，并直接走向底楼的一间后屋，“哈瓦斯”通讯社的无线电报发射台即设于此。

(1) 俄国辅助警员 18-247 - 中国警员 927-939
及安南巡捕 420。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Pendant que le nommé CHANG CHIH FAN, armé d'un pis-
tolet (1) tenait le coolie YANG NING KENG, sous la menace
de son arme, son complice enlevait 4 lampes du poste d'émis-
sion et plaçait, à l'intérieur de l'appareil, une boîte
à cigarettes contenant un explosif ? -

Ces diverses opérations terminées, tous deux sont
partis en emmenant le coolie. A un moment donné, ce der-
nier, ayant réussi à se sauver, donna l'alarme à des agents,
qui, après poursuite, procédèrent à l'arrestation des deux
fugitifs.

Interrogés, les nommés CHANG CHIH FAN et LI DAH ZIE,
nous ont déclaré ce qui suit :
Le premier est un ex-membre du Tangpu central de
Nankin du Gouvernement national; et de la section de pro-
pagande du Parti Kuomintang à Chungking.
Le deuxième est un ex-traducteur de télégrammes du
journal "Ming Kuo Jih Pao" - fermé dès le début des hos-
tilités.
Tous deux sont actuellement employés comme membres
stagiaires, depuis deux mois, au No 76 Jessfield Road,
sous les ordres d'un nommé SZE TAH YU (施大愚), subor-
donné de TING ME TSUENG (丁默). Ils n'ont d'après eux,
aucune affectation ni mission déterminées.
C'est SZE TAH YU qui leur a donné l'ordre hier, de
se rendre à la station "Havas", et c'est également lui
qui leur a remis ce matin le pistolet et la grenade. L'ins-
tigateur leur aurait déclaré que ce poste était une agence
d'informations du Gouvernement national.
Hier, vers 19 heures, sous la conduite de SZE, le
nommé LI DAH ZI est allé reconnaître les lieux.

(1) Browning Herstal belgique No 552084 nanti d'un chargeur
de 7 cartouches. Pas d'antécédents sur la C.F.

前者系南京国民政府中央党部及国民党重庆宣传部的前成员。
后者系《民国日报》的前电报翻译员——该报自战事爆发之初即已关闭。

SECRET

H. Q. C. B.    6813/16
August 29, 30 38. 39

LETTER OF WARNING RECEIVED BY AMERICAN CITIZEN.

D.S.I. Crighton        D.I. Glover

Sir,

At 3.45 p.m. 28-8-39, Mr. A. R. Lusey, American
Citizen, Far Eastern Manager of the Press Wireless Inc.,
Room 901, Hamilton House, 103 Kiukiang Road, called at Crime
Branch Headquarters (C. 1.), bringing with him a letter which
he had found in the letter box of his office at 12.10 p.m.
28-8-39.

From a perusal of this letter (attached) it would
appear that same had been sent in the nature of a warning and
Mr. Lusey, when questioned regarding same, gave the following
information.

Approximately nine years ago on the inauguration
of the Dollar Radio Station, which Mr. Lusey supervised the
building of, the Chinese Minister of Communications gave a
dinner party, and whilst attending this Mr. Lusey was introduced
to a thin, rather well-to-do Chinese youth who had recently
returned from America. During the course of the evening Mr.
Lusey struck up an acquaintance with this young man, and as a
result ascertained that he had been studying radio in America.
Some days later, this youth ( name either Sung ( ) or Chow
( ) ) approached him, with a view to getting a job with the
Chinese Government, and through the Minister of Communications
Mr. Lusey was successful in obtaining a position for him in
the China National Airways Corp., however after being employed
therein for four months, this youth left and since then until
quite recently Mr. Lusey has seen nothing of him.

On or about the 17th July 1939, Mr. Lusey was
accosted by this male Chinese, who explained that he was now

（印：SECRET）
（批：R.C.J. 29/8）

总部刑事处
刑事情报杂项档案
第743/39号
日期 1939年8月29日

机密

总部刑事处    6813/16
1938年8月29、30日. 1939年

美国公民收到警告信。

副督察 赖顿        督察 格洛弗

先生，

1939年8月28日下午3时45分，美国公民、Press Wireless Inc.远东经理A. R. Lusey先生来到刑事处总部（C. 1.），地址为九江路103号汉密尔顿大厦901室。他带来了一封信，该信是他于1939年8月28日中午12时10分在其办公室信箱中发现的。

阅读这封信（见附件）后可知，此信性质上属于警告。就此事询问Lusey先生时，他提供了以下信息。

大约九年前，在Lusey先生监督建设的美元电台落成之际，中国交通部长举行晚宴，Lusey先生在出席期间被介绍给一位刚从美国回来的、身材瘦削且相当富裕的中国青年。当晚，Lusey先生与这位年轻人结识，并得知他在美国学习过无线电技术。几天后，这位青年（名字可能是宋（Sung）或周（Chow））为了在中国政府谋职而接近他，通过交通部长，Lusey先生成功为他在中国航空公司获得了一个职位，然而在该处工作四个月后，这名青年离职，此后直到最近，Lusey先生再未见过他。

1939年7月17日左右，Lusey先生被这名中国男子拦住，对方解释说他现在

（印：机密）
（批：R.C.J. 8月29日）

page_data.en:
- 2 -

employed as a wireless operator for the Japanese and that he
was operating a receiving station which was picking up all
messages being relayed by the Press Wireless Inc. and Globe
Wireless Inc., and that the Japanese were very annoyed with
the messages he had been transmitting particularly those
referring to Sgt. Kinloch. He then warned Mr. Lusey to be
careful, and at the same time expressed the desire to get back
with the Ministry of Communications for the Nationalist
Government, saying he was fed up working for the Japanese.

On this occasion Mr. Lusey requested this man to
call on him at his office but this was refused.

In explaining the "Kinloch" affair Mr. Lusey
explained that the Japanese had complained to his head office
in New York regarding the messages sent by him and had
threatened that unless such ceased immediately they would
interrupt the Tokyo - San Francisco circuit.

This warning was ignored by the home office and
the matter more or less was forgotten.

In continuing, Mr. Lusey explained that for some
time past he had been attempting to inaugurate a Chungking -
Shanghai direct circuit and that through a Mr. "A", who was
i/c of the local Nationalist Government Radio Station, he had
met with a fair amount of success.

Whether or not this had become known to the
Japanese he could not say, but there was every possibility
that it had, and that this again had raised their ire.

Referring to the paragraph which relates to the
late Mr. R. P. Krogh, Mr. Lusey states that same is nonsense,
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

受雇于日本人担任无线电操作员，正在运营一个接收站，截获Press Wireless Inc.和Globe Wireless Inc.中继的所有信息，而且日本人对他传输的信息非常恼火，特别是那些提及Kinloch警长的信息。随后他警告Lusey先生要小心，同时表示希望回到国民政府交通部任职，称他为日本人工作已经受够了。

当时，Lusey先生要求此人到他的办公室来谈，但被拒绝。

在解释“Kinloch”事件时，Lusey先生说明，日本人曾就他发送的信息向其在纽约的总公司投诉，并威胁除非立即停止，否则他们将中断东京至旧金山的线路。

总公司忽视了这一警告，此事也就大致被遗忘了。

Lusey先生继续解释说，一段时间以来，他一直试图开通重庆至上海的直达线路，并通过负责当地国民政府电台的“A”先生取得了一定的成功。

日本人是否知晓此事他无法确定，但极有可能已经知晓，这再次激怒了日本人。

关于涉及已故R. P. Krogh先生的段落，Lusey先生称那是无稽之谈，

page_data.en:
- 3 -

inasmuch as that the Nationalist Government require no
assistance from any foreign radio station, they themselves
having one of the most efficient private stations in Shanghai,
also that he had already enquired regarding this point through
Mr. "A" and had received a negative reply.

In referring to the letter which he received,
Mr. Lusey stated that in his opinion it could only mean one of
two things, either that the male Chinese whom he had befriended
years ago was giving him a genuine warning or that the whole
thing was a bluff on part of this man, who, as already mentioned,
had voiced the opinion that he wished to return to the Ministry
of Communications under the Nationalist Government.

Questioned as to whether or not he could locate
this man, Mr. Lusey explained that the only hope he had of doing

Reference the attached memo. giving certain
details of a radio station, call sign K. A. Z. I.,
alleged by the Japanese to be operating in the Western
district of the Settlement, enquiries made by the Special
Branch ascertained that the station referred to is a
receiving and transmitting station located in Room 321
of 749 Bubbling Well Road, which is the property of
Bentleys Limited, an American concern operated by
Mr. S.V. MARCO (registered American), Room 216, Chartered
Bank Building, 18 The Bund. The station suspended
operations some four days ago, apparently due to the
owner having become aware that enquiries were being made
concerning it.

Information received from a reliable and
confidential source revealed that Bentleys Ltd. was
formed with the full unofficial support of the local
and Tientsin American Chambers of Commerce, for the
purpose of undertaking the transmitting of messages to
Chengtu via Tientsin in order to avoid the Japanese
enforced censorship. From Chengtu messages may be
relayed to places abroad via Manila or other points.
It is known that unofficially, the American Consulate-
General officials are fully cognizant of all details
relating to the operations of Bentleys Ltd., but for
certain reasons, prefer not to recognise the concern
officially.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 5 1939

Hot Radio Chestnut

IN PROTESTING against the operation in Shanghai of an American radio communications company licensed by the Chinese and the United States Governments, the Japanese have chosen to seize an extremely hot chestnut. Before they are through with it they may wish they had continued to let it lie.

The protest is said to be based on two points—first, that the company's license in China was "obtained from Chungking", and second, that it operates "without the supervision of the Japanese authorities." How much merit is there in these points?

By international agreement every country exercises sovereignty over radio within its borders. Japan was one of the subscribers to this principle. It will be recalled that a few years ago Shanghai's radio broadcasting chaos was settled on a basis of this convention. With no dissenting voice, it was agreed that the National Government had full right to control radio even within the foreign areas of Shanghai, and therefore all stations, even within the Settlement and Concession and even foreign-owned and operated stations, changed their call letters and wave lengths in accordance with the instructions of the proper organ of the National Government.

Whatever Tokyo may think of that National Government, it continues to exist and to be the only recognized Government of China. Even Japan herself has not yet recognised her pitiful puppet creations which squabble among themselves, hide from the public view, and make no slightest pretense of governing, although it is to be presumed that Tokyo will extend recognition as soon as there is the slightest opportunity or excuse.

It is clearly the obligation of any communications company to obtain its license for China operation from the National Government and this Globe Wireless has done. How Washington can be expected to construe this as wrong it is quite impossible for us to fathom. On the contrary, it would seem to be Washington's obvious duty to support this or any other company which has complied with the requirements of both the Chinese and the American duly constituted authorities.

As to the issue of accepting "supervision of the Japanese authorities," it can only be said that American companies lie under no obligation whatever to accept such supervision if they choose not to do so. If they elect to tolerate such supervision, as a practical matter of expediency, that is their business, just as it would be their business if they developed such a high regard for the writer that they invited him to supervise their operations. Nobody happens to have thought of or acted upon our second possibility, and Globe Wireless finds the first without appeal. It's all up to Globe and we hardly see Uncle Sam intruding into such an intimate phase of the company's business.

The reason this whole question is a super-heated chestnut lies in Japan's own bold ventures into the China communications field. Among other things, the Chenju radio station, formerly owned and operated by the Chinese Government, has been taken over by the Japanese and is being used by various parties with the station under their administration. So long as neither Chungking nor any third party raises the issue, it may be tacitly assumed that things merely go on as they did before the war. But we know this is not really the case and if the Japanese insist upon a ruling concerning Globe's operation of its own station (which it has every right to do in China if the Chinese give permission, as they have) they may blunder into a parallel ruling most uncomfortable to their present set-up.

We don't say that such a thing should happen or that it will; but the Japanese are taking a chance when they stir things up. So far as Globe is concerned, what does Japan want the United States to do—tear up the international radio convention? America has shown very little inclination to emulate Japan in such issues.

1939年1月5日

烫手的栗子

在抗议一家获中国和美国政府许可的美国无线电通信公司在上海运营时，日本人选择捡起了一颗极其烫手的栗子。在他们彻底解决此事之前，他们可能会希望自己当初让它继续躺在那里。

据说这一抗议基于两点——第一，该公司在中国的许可证是“从重庆获得的”；第二，其运营“不受日本当局监管”。这两点有多少道理？

根据国际协定，每个国家对其境内的无线电行使主权。日本是该原则的签署国之一。人们会记得，几年前上海无线电广播的混乱局面就是基于这一公约得以解决的。当时毫无异议地达成一致，即国民政府拥有充分的权利控制甚至上海外侨区域内的无线电，因此所有电台，即使在租界和公界内，甚至是外资拥有和运营的电台，都按照国民政府主管机关的指示更改了其呼号和波长。

无论东京对该国民政府有何看法，它依然存在，并且是中国唯一被承认的政府。就连日本自己也尚未承认那些相互争吵、躲避公众视线、丝毫不假装进行治理的可怜傀儡政权，尽管可以推测，只要有一丝机会或借口，东京就会予以承认。

任何通信公司都有义务从国民政府获得在中国运营的许可证，而 Globe Wireless（环球无线电公司）已经这样做了。华盛顿怎么会认为这是错误的，我们根本无法理解。相反，支持这家或任何其他符合中美两国正式组建当局要求的公司，似乎是华盛顿显而易见的责任。

至于接受“日本当局监管”的问题，只能说，如果美国公司选择不接受，它们没有任何义务接受这种监管。如果它们出于实际权宜之计选择容忍这种监管，那是它们自己的事，就像如果它们对笔者产生如此高的敬意而邀请笔者监管其运营一样，那也是它们自己的事。碰巧没有人想到或采取我们的第二种可能性，而 Globe Wireless 发现第一种情况没有上诉余地。这完全取决于 Globe 公司，我们几乎看不出山姆大叔会干涉该公司业务中如此私密的阶段。

整个问题之所以成为一颗超高温的栗子，原因在于日本自身大胆涉足中国通信领域。其中，原由中国政府拥有和运营的陈如（Chenju，音译）无线电台已被日本人接管，并由各方在该台的管理下使用。只要重庆或任何第三方不提出这一问题，就可以默许事情像战前那样继续下去。但我们知道事实并非如此，如果日本人坚持要对 Globe 公司运营其自有电台（如果中国人给予许可，正如他们所做的那样，它在中国完全有权这样做）做出裁决，他们可能会笨拙地陷入一个对其现有体制极为不适的平行裁决中。

我们不是说这种事情应该发生或将会发生；但当日本人搅动局势时，他们是在冒险。就 Globe 公司而言，日本希望美国做什么——撕毁国际无线电公约吗？在此类问题上，美国表现出很少有意效仿日本。
